newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF slaps penalties on Nomura for payoff scandal.
newsitem.headline: MOF slaps penalties on Nomura for payoff scandal.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Wednesday it ordered Nomura Securities Co Ltd to halt its own-account stock-related dealing, including options and index trading, from August 6 to December 31.

MOF said in a statement it will also suspend Nomura's stock-related business at all branches from August 6 to August 12, while securities trading and securities futures broking at the first corporate division at Nomura headquarters will be suspended from August 6 to December 5.
The first corporate division is one of two such divisions at Nomura, and is the department that managed an account linked to a "sokaiya" racketeer.
The head office as a whole, excluding the first corporate division, will be suspended from securities trading and securities futures broking from August 6 to September 5.

Nomura will also be barred from participating in the auction and underwriting of public bonds, including Japanese government bonds (JGBs), municipal bonds and government-guaranteed bonds, from August 6 to December 31.
MOF also ordered Nomura to draw up a report by September 19 that would:
* identify steps Nomura will take to strengthen internal management structures
* identify steps to improve staff compliance with laws and regulations
* provide a review of trading operations within the company
* clarify responsibility for actions at Nomura that made it difficult for facts to surface
* identify steps Nomura will take to cut ties with "anti-social forces", including sokaiya.
